Molecular graphs from atoms and bonds

Source: R/molecules.R
molecule_graph.Rd

molecule_graph() builds an undirected graph_data() object with one node per atom and one edge pair per bond. Node features are a one hot encoding of the element over elements (an extra "other" column catches anything else); edge features are a one hot encoding of the bond order over bond_orders, repeated for both directions.

Usage

molecule_graph(
  atoms,
  bonds,
  elements = c("C", "N", "O", "S", "F", "Cl", "Br", "P", "I"),
  bond_orders = c(1, 2, 3, 1.5),
  graph_y = NULL
)

dataset_synthetic_molecules(n = 100L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

atoms

Character vector of element symbols.

bonds

Integer matrix or data frame with columns from, to (1 based atom positions) and optionally order (bond order, default 1).

elements

Elements given their own feature column.

bond_orders

Bond orders given their own feature column (1.5 for aromatic).

graph_y

Optional graph label.

n

Number of molecules.

seed

Optional seed; the caller's random stream is left untouched.

Value

molecule_graph(): a graph_data object. dataset_synthetic_molecules(): a list of them with a "scaffold" attribute.

Details

graphlearnR does not parse SMILES or compute Bemis-Murcko scaffolds; use a chemistry toolkit such as RDKit for that and pass atoms, bonds and scaffold identifiers here and to split_graphs().

dataset_synthetic_molecules() generates small random molecules: a carbon backbone, optionally closed into a ring of 5 or 6 atoms, with random heteroatoms (N, O) and side chains. The label graph_y is "ring" or "chain", and the list's "scaffold" attribute holds a synthetic scaffold identifier per molecule (ring size and heteroatom count in the ring) so that scaffold splits can be demonstrated. The data are synthetic and carry no chemical meaning.

Examples

# ethanol, heavy atoms only
g <- molecule_graph(c("C", "C", "O"), rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)))
g
#> <graph_data> undirected graph: 3 nodes, 4 edges (2 undirected pairs)
#>   node features [3 x 10]
#>   edge features [4 x 4]
mols <- dataset_synthetic_molecules(20, seed = 1)
table(vapply(mols, function(m) as.character(m$graph_y), ""))
#> 
#> chain  ring 
#>    10    10
